validity.recommendation: The row is a real pipeline and not a duplicate. It is one of two lines of TurkStream. Most figures in the wiki list are for both lines together, so per-line capacity and cost are not backed by them.
validity.researcher_notes: The 31.5 billion cubic metre capacity and the 7.8 billion dollar cost belong to the whole project. The sheet has 15.75 on each line, which is half of 31.5, and 7.8 billion dollars on this row only. Neither is stated per line in the pages read.

fills.researcher_notes: The TurkStream project site says each of the two offshore pipelines is 930 kilometres long. The Wikipedia article on TurkStream gives 930 kilometres as well.
The Wikipedia article says both lines use pipe with an outer diameter of 810 millimetres, which it also gives as 32 inches. The sheet value of 813 millimetres is the same 32 inch pipe.
The Wikipedia article gives 8 January 2020 as the commissioning date of TurkStream. The RFE/RL report also says the inauguration ceremony was set for 8 January. The article covers both lines.
The Wikipedia article says TurkStream was commissioned on 8 January 2020 and describes gas deliveries through both lines since then, including 2023 volumes.

The pages in the wiki list give 31.5 billion cubic metres a year for both lines together. None states 15.75 for one line. A system figure is not a source for one line, so the value was left without a source this pass. Not searched beyond the wiki list.

The wiki pages say South Stream Transport B.V., a Gazprom subsidiary, built the project. None says who owns this pipeline, so Gazprom PJSC at 100 percent has no source this pass. Not searched beyond the wiki list.
The only cost the wiki pages give is a figure for the whole two-line project, 7.8 billion dollars from RFE/RL. It is already on the first line row, so it was not repeated here.
The Wikipedia article names Gazprom as operator of the offshore section and the Russian onshore section, and BOTAS for the Turkish onshore section. Gazprom operates the offshore pipe.
